stem: Which facial feature is part of the diagnostic triad of fetal alcohol syndrome?
explanation: Smooth philtrum is one of the classic facial features of fetal alcohol syndrome.
rationale: The diagnostic facial triad includes short palpebral fissures, a smooth philtrum, and a thin upper vermilion.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because fetal alcohol syndrome is associated with short palpebral fissures rather than upslanting palpebral fissures.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because a smooth philtrum is one of the classic facial features of fetal alcohol syndrome.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a single central incisor is associated with holoprosencephaly, not the characteristic fetal alcohol syndrome facial triad.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a bifid uvula is not part of the typical diagnostic triad of fetal alcohol syndrome.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a thin upper lip is a feature of fetal alcohol syndrome, but the classic triad specifically includes the smooth philtrum instead.

source.hint: This feature relates to the vertical groove between the base of the nose and the border of the upper lip.
